Coerce Spatial Objects to a Bounding Box in a Target CRS

Source: R/spatial_dispatch.R
vantor_as_bbox.Rd

S3 generic function that extracts a bounding box from spatial objects across major R geography packages (sf, terra, stars) or numeric vectors and transforms it to a target Coordinate Reference System (CRS).

Usage

vantor_as_bbox(x, target_crs = 3857, source_crs = NULL, ...)

Arguments

x

A spatial object (sf, sfc, bbox, SpatRaster, SpatVector, SpatExtent, stars, stars_proxy) or a numeric vector of length 4: c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax).

target_crs

Integer or character string. Target EPSG code or CRS definition. Default is 3857 (Web Mercator).

source_crs

Integer or character string. Source CRS used only when x is a plain numeric vector without a "crs" attribute. If NULL, heuristically detects EPSG:4326 if coordinates fall within valid longitude/latitude bounds ([-180, 180] and [-90, 90]), or EPSG:3857 otherwise.

...

Additional arguments passed to methods.

Value

An sf bbox object (c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax)) in target_crs.

Examples

# From a lat/lon numeric vector (automatically detected as EPSG:4326)
vantor_as_bbox(c(-105.01, 39.72, -104.96, 39.75), target_crs = 3857)
#>      xmin      ymin      xmax      ymax 
#> -11689660   4825336 -11684094   4829679 

# From an sf bbox object
bb <- sf::st_bbox(c(xmin = -77.04, ymin = 38.88, xmax = -77.03, ymax = 38.89),
                  crs = sf::st_crs(4326))
vantor_as_bbox(bb, target_crs = 3857)
#>     xmin     ymin     xmax     ymax 
#> -8576054  4704497 -8574940  4705927
